newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares shed 0.81 pct in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares shed 0.81 pct in thin volume.

text.p: Istanbul shares lost an average 0.81 percent in quiet selling on Monday as traders took profits in thin volume after last week's 6.2 percent jump, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed at 94,107.12, down 772.02 points, or 0.81 percent from Friday's all-time high closing of 94,879.14. Trade volume dived to 12.96 trillion lira ($121.6 million) from Friday's 19.30 trillion ($182.1 million).

Brokers said the market awaited the Treasury's 13-month bond auction set for Tuesday to see developments in financial markets. Bond market yields had dived in the two days following last Tuesday's auction where the Treasury succeeded in issuing first ever 13-month bonds at sharply lower yields.
"Investors may want to keep liquidity ahead of the year-end. The issue of a five-day New Year holiday remains uncertain," said Haydar Haydaroglu from Halkbank.
The Turkish government may extend the New Year holiday to five days from December 27 to January 2 by declaring December 30 and 31 official holiday.

"If the holiday is extended, there may be purchases in the last two days of the week because payments will be delayed until after the holiday. If the market establishes firm support at 94,000 levels, an upward move is also possible," Haydaroglu said.
